topic: General Name Lookup Process with ADL in C++
explanation: Name lookup in C++ is a complex process significantly impacting compilation and runtime behavior.  It involves a sequence of steps, starting with the immediate scope and extending outwards.  Argument-Dependent Lookup (ADL), also known as Koenig lookup, is a crucial aspect, influencing function overload resolution based on the types of arguments provided.  Understanding ADL is essential for predicting which function overload will be selected, especially when dealing with templates and namespaces. The compiler uses sophisticated algorithms to perform this lookup, often involving symbol tables and intricate parsing of the code.  Memory layout is not directly affected, but the chosen function impacts the memory accessed during execution. Incorrect or ambiguous name lookup can result in compiler errors or runtime crashes.
keywords: ADL, Koenig lookup, C++ name lookup, Argument dependent lookup
